stories.title: Tech giants' energy demands are 'crazy,' says SA premier
stories.summary: South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas says the world’s biggest technology companies have unrealistic expectations about the energy available to power their artificial intelligence aspirations in…
stories.title_zh: 南澳州州长称科技巨头的能源需求"疯狂"
stories.content:
South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas says the world’s biggest technology companies have unrealistic expectations about the energy available to power their artificial intelligence aspirations in Australia, warning there is nowhere near enough renewable generation.

Malinauskas, who travelled to the United States in July to meet with AI developers and data centre operators, along with Democrats and Republicans, said demand for power was “just crazy stuff”.

stories.title: NextDC under siege as Goodman and Digital Realty snap up 9.9pc stake
stories.summary: Goodman Group and Digital Realty have collectively acquired a 9.9 percent stake in Australian operator NextDC, fueling speculation about strategic intentions and potential control battles. The investment comes as Australian data centre assets attract heightened global interest.
stories.why_it_matters: The 9.9 percent threshold is deliberately below Australia's foreign investment review trigger, suggesting coordinated positioning ahead of a potential full bid or joint venture. NextDC's management now faces compressed strategic options: negotiate with two powerful suitors simultaneously, seek a white knight, or accelerate organic expansion to demonstrate standalone value before either party can accumulate more shares.
stories.title_zh: NextDC遭围攻，Goodman和Digital Realty抢购9.9%股份
stories.summary_zh: Goodman Group 和 Digital Realty 共同收购了澳大利亚运营商 NextDC 9.9% 的股份，引发了对战略意图和潜在控制权争夺的猜测。此次投资正值澳大利亚数据中心资产吸引全球高度关注之际。
stories.why_zh: 9.9% 的门槛故意低于澳大利亚外国投资审查触发点，表明在潜在全面收购或合资企业之前进行协调布局。NextDC 管理层现在面临压缩的战略选择：同时与两个强大的竞购方谈判、寻找白衣骑士，或在任何一方积累更多股份之前加速有机扩张以证明独立价值。
stories.content:
NextDC chief executive Craig Scroggie says he takes responsibility for the firestorm engulfing the data centre operator and vowed to fix the energy problems holding up its Melbourne development, after a shock earnings downgrade last month pummelled the company’s share price and opened the door to an opportunistic raid on its register.

Addressing a packed room at the UBS Australasia Conference in Sydney on Monday afternoon, Scroggie said he was “deeply sorry” for the impact on the community and customers, acknowledging they felt they’d been “left behind”.

stories.title: Keep coal firing and start up nuclear to power data centres
stories.summary: Energy analysts and some policymakers are advocating extended coal plant operations alongside nuclear power development to meet data centre baseload requirements. The proposal challenges prevailing decarbonization timelines in markets where renewable intermittency remains unresolved.
stories.why_it_matters: Data centre operators' net-zero commitments are colliding with physical reality: batteries cannot yet bridge multi-day renewable lulls at hyperscale, and small modular reactors remain years from commercial deployment. The coal-nuclear argument forces a sector-wide reckoning—either relax near-term carbon targets, pay massive premiums for firming capacity, or accept slower expansion in markets with strict emissions rules.
stories.title_zh: 维持煤炭发电并启动核电以为数据中心供电
stories.summary_zh: 能源分析师和部分政策制定者主张延长煤电运营并发展核电，以满足数据中心的 baseload 需求。这一提议在可再生能源间歇性问题仍未解决的市场中，对 prevailing decarbonization 时间表构成挑战。
stories.why_zh: 数据中心运营商的净零承诺正与物理现实碰撞：电池尚无法在 hyperscale 层面弥补可再生能源多日低谷，小型模块化反应堆距离商业部署仍有数年。煤电-核电的论点迫使全行业正视现实——要么放宽近期碳目标，为 firming capacity 支付巨额溢价，要么在排放规则严格的市场接受更缓慢的扩张。
stories.content:
Federal parliament will make a series of important decisions over the coming months that will help define national standards for large artificial intelligence data centres.

Australia is competing for some of the largest capital investments ever made, as the hyperscalers and AI labs decide where to build. We need to think seriously about how Australia participates in the AI revolution because the choices we make now will shape our society, economy, and environment for many decades ahead.

stories.title: Mitsui Chemicals to take over chip linchpin JSR for US$12 bil
stories.summary: (Nov 9): Japan’s Mitsui Chemicals Inc is buying JSR Corp for ¥1.84 trillion (US$12 billion) with support from state-backed Development Bank of Japan (DBJ) to strengthen its hold over a key chip materials linchpin.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.title_zh: 三井化学将以120亿美元收购芯片关键企业JSR
stories.content:
Mitsui Chemicals and DBJ will acquire all shares of JSR from government-backed Japan Investment Corp, the companies said in a filing Monday. DBJ will pay ¥200 billion in cash for a stake that will be converted to preferred shares without voting rights, it said.

The deal for JSR, one of the world’s leading makers of photoresists needed to make advanced chips, would further a government-backed effort to consolidate Japan’s fragmented semiconductor-materials industry. Japan is home to the world’s largest suppliers of silicon wafers and dominates several other critical chip materials, but many of its smaller suppliers remain vulnerable to foreign takeovers.

Mitsui Chemicals’ shares extended their decline to as much as 15% in Tokyo.

JIC took JSR private two years ago. JSR supplies light-sensitive materials used with ASML Holding NV’s extreme ultraviolet lithography machines to pattern fine circuits onto silicon wafers. Customers for JSR’s array of specialty chemicals include Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, Intel Corp and Samsung Electronics Co, according to data compiled by *Bloomberg*.

*Bloomberg News* reported in September that JSR was weighing buyout proposals from Mitsui Chemicals and rival Mitsubishi Chemical Group Corp.

stories.title: RBA's Hunter says AI boom will put near-term pressure on CPI
stories.summary: (Nov 9): A senior official at Australia’s central bank said surging investment in areas related to artificial intelligence will further fuel demand in the economy, at a time when policymakers are already aggressively raising interest rates to combat inflation.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.title_zh: 澳联储Hunter称AI繁荣将对CPI造成短期压力
stories.content:
(Nov 9): A senior official at Australia’s central bank said surging investment in areas related to artificial intelligence will further fuel demand in the economy, at a time when policymakers are already aggressively raising interest rates to combat inflation.

In a speech on the potential impact of AI, Reserve Bank assistant governor Sarah Hunter on Monday called it among “the most significant technological developments of our time,” one already beginning to reshape the economy.

“In the near term, the positive shock to aggregate demand set against the economy’s current supply capacity will put some upward pressure on inflation,” she said. “Some liaison contacts are reporting that data centre construction is adding to demand for some already-stretched construction skilled trades.”

Rising construction costs are one channel AI demand is feeding through to the consumer price index, Hunter said during a Q&A after her speech. To a lesser extent, price rises for newer mobile phones and game consoles are also boosting the CPI, she added.

Australia’s construction project pipeline reached a record A$1.4 trillion through September and may end up double the scale of the mining boom, according to Deloitte Access Economics. Both the RBA and government have pointed out the surprising strength of business investment, even as the US-Iran war has pushed energy prices higher and weighed on households.

Still, risks to the AI project pipeline are “balanced,” Hunter said in response to a question, pointing out that potential changes to regulation could crimp some developments.

The RBA has raised interest rates five times this year to 4.85%, an 18-year high, as it struggles to regain control over inflation.

On the upside, once initial bottlenecks are overcome, AI is expected to boost productivity because economies will be able to produce more with the same inputs. That suggests the initial inflationary pressures will dissipate in time, Hunter said in her speech, while acknowledging high uncertainty over the scale of gains.

“Current estimates for the impact of AI on annual productivity growth over the next decade range from over 2% to just 0.1%,” she said.

While Hunter said AI is likely to change the labour market significantly in time, to date it has been fairly muted.

“Contacts in the RBA’s liaison program indicate that AI has not yet impacted most firms’ headcount and is not expected to over the next year,” Hunter said.

“However, there are tentative signs of adjustment, through weaker job ad posting and employment outcomes in more AI-exposed occupations, and stronger growth in areas where the technology has had less of an impact, particularly for younger workers,” she said.

Global financial markets were whipsawed last week after the Democratic Party’s sweep of Congress in the US midterm elections, which stoked fear among investors about tighter regulation of the data center industry.

Hunter said the exposure of financial market participants to the AI investment boom is increasing at a time when investors are demanding very little compensation for taking on risky assets.

“If the returns to AI investment disappoint, some asset prices, including equities and corporate debt, will be exposed to sharp repricing and possibly disorderly adjustments,” she said.

stories.title: Malaysia-Taiwan fraying ties threaten future chip investments
stories.summary: Diplomatic tensions between Malaysia and Taiwan are creating uncertainty for semiconductor investment flows, with potential implications for chip packaging and advanced manufacturing projects. The friction complicates supply chain planning in a critical node for the global chip industry.
stories.why_it_matters: Taiwanese chip firms have increasingly looked to Malaysia as a diversification hedge against China risk, but political friction could redirect billions in planned investment to Vietnam, India or Japan. Malaysian policymakers now face a delicate balancing act: maintaining informal Taiwan ties that attract technology transfer without triggering Beijing's retaliation that could damage broader economic relationships.

stories.summary_zh: 马来西亚与台湾之间的外交紧张局势正为半导体投资流动带来不确定性，可能对 chip packaging 和先进制造项目产生影响。这一摩擦使全球芯片产业关键节点的供应链规划变得复杂。
stories.why_zh: 台湾芯片企业越来越多地将马来西亚视为对冲中国风险的多元化选择，但政治摩擦可能使数十亿美元的规划投资转向越南、印度或日本。马来西亚政策制定者现在面临微妙的平衡：维持能吸引技术转让的非正式台湾关系，同时避免触发可能损害更广泛经济关系的中国报复。

stories.title: Taiwan, South Korea, Japan stock markets hit hard by AI sell-off
stories.summary: Equity markets in Taiwan, South Korea and Japan experienced significant declines as investors rotated away from AI-related stocks amid broader valuation concerns. The sell-off affected semiconductor manufacturers, component suppliers and data centre-adjacent companies across the region.
stories.why_it_matters: APAC markets have become a leveraged proxy for AI demand sentiment, with Korean memory and Taiwanese foundry stocks magnifying moves in US semiconductor equities. The synchronized decline suggests regional investors are questioning whether AI infrastructure spending growth rates can sustain current multiples, which directly threatens the funding environment for data centre expansion projects dependent on equity-linked capital.
stories.title_zh: 台湾、韩国、日本股市因AI抛售遭受重创
stories.summary_zh: 台湾、韩国和日本的股市出现大幅下跌，投资者在更广泛的估值担忧中从 AI 相关股票轮换撤出。此次抛售影响了该地区的半导体制造商、零部件供应商和数据中心相关企业。
stories.why_zh: 亚太市场已成为 AI 需求情绪的杠杆代理，韩国存储器和台湾代工股票的波动放大了美国半导体股票的变动。同步下跌表明区域投资者正在质疑 AI 基础设施支出增长率能否支撑当前估值倍数，这直接威胁到依赖股权关联资本的数据中心扩张项目的融资环境。
stories.content: TOKYO -- Asian stock markets tied to the artificial intelligence boom plummeted on Friday following a tech sell-off on Wall Street overnight, as investors fretted about possible delays in the construction of data centers following a sweeping Democratic victory in the U.S. midterm elections.

stories.title: Keppel's real AI story isn't the humanoid robot
stories.summary: Keppel has deployed agentic AI systems that autonomously evaluate data centre site selection and predict equipment failures, generating operational returns ahead of its more publicized humanoid robotics initiatives. The technology is already reducing downtime and accelerating development timelines.
stories.why_it_matters: Agentic AI for site selection and predictive maintenance commoditizes expertise that previously justified premium consulting fees and long senior-staff tenures. If Keppel's systems prove transferable, smaller operators and new market entrants can match incumbent decision quality without comparable institutional knowledge, potentially eroding the competitive moat of established players like Equinix and Digital Realty.

stories.why_zh: 用于选址和预测性维护的 agentic AI 正在使此前支撑高额咨询费和资深员工长期任职的专业知识商品化。如果 Keppel 的系统被证明可转移，较小运营商和新进入者可以在不具备同等机构知识的情况下匹敌 incumbents 的决策质量，可能侵蚀 Equinix 和 Digital Realty 等 established players 的竞争护城河。
stories.content:
Keppel’s agentic AI that picks data centre sites and spots breakdowns is already paying its way

\[SINGAPORE\] When Keppel trots its embodied artificial intelligence robots into the room, it feels like stepping into a futuristic movie set.

Ken the humanoid greets visitors by name, while a robot dog called Sentry sweeps the room and flags something odd, right on cue. The cameras love it.

Ken is being trained to flip high-voltage switches at the Senoko waste-to-energy plant. Sniff, another robot dog, is meant to crawl into incinerators and test the air for toxic gas.

stories.title: Dell expands AI factory with NVIDIA for agentic AI
stories.summary: More than 6,500 customers have adopted Dell's AI Factory with NVIDIA as it adds deskside systems, servers and managed services for agentic AI.
stories.title_zh: Dell与NVIDIA扩展AI factory以支持agentic AI
stories.content:
Dell has expanded its Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA with new software, deskside systems and data-centre infrastructure for agentic AI. More than 6,500 customers have adopted the offering.

The update includes validated models and software, managed services, desktop and workstation configurations, modular data-centre designs and new PowerEdge servers for organisations running AI workloads on their own infrastructure.

Dell is positioning the package around a growing enterprise push to move agentic AI projects beyond the pilot stage. It said businesses want greater control over data, operations and costs as they deploy AI agents more widely across development teams, office environments and core infrastructure.

Among the software additions, Reflection's Beam open-weight model has been validated on the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA. Dell also added or updated ecosystem programme solutions for AI observability with Dynatrace, a knowledge assistant and agentic AI platform with Mistral, and computer vision with Fogsphere.

SUSE Linux will be added as an operating system option for the stack. Dell also outlined a layered security approach combining Dell infrastructure, the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for runtime governance and Red Hat AI Factory software for orchestration.

Alongside the platform changes, Dell introduced Dell Managed Services for AI. The service is intended to help customers govern access to AI resources, manage consumption and monitor costs as projects move from early trials into broader operational use.

### Deskside systems

Dell also expanded its deskside agentic AI offering, reflecting its view that AI workloads will increasingly be distributed between central infrastructure and systems used by individual developers and teams.

The expansion includes new validated reference deployment templates for Dell Deskside Agentic AI Solutions for NVIDIA. Dell said the templates set out the hardware, models and software stack for uses including agentic coding, agentic VSS, NVIDIA NemoClaw, Hermes Agent on NemoClaw and a higher education AI lab platform.

According to Dell, the templates are designed to scale from a single developer system to deployments of 1,000 or more systems. It also introduced a 64GB unified memory configuration for Dell Pro Precision with GB10, aimed at individual developers and smaller teams working on local agentic AI development.

The desktop can be linked in clusters of two or four systems to support larger models and more complex workflows. Dell also said Dell Pro Precision with GB300 will be offered with Windows, bringing up to 748GB of coherent memory and 20 petaflops of FP4 compute to deskside environments already managed by enterprise IT teams.

### Data-centre buildout

In the data centre, Dell announced a modular reference design called the Dell Modular Data Centre with NVIDIA DSX POD. The containerised design includes compute, storage, networking, rack-level power and liquid cooling, and is intended to reduce on-site integration work by allowing connection to prepared power infrastructure.

Dell also detailed several new server platforms. The Dell PowerEdge M9882 is a CPU-focused system that places 256 NVIDIA Vera CPUs in a single 48U rack for workloads such as orchestration, tool use, code execution and evaluation alongside GPU-based inference systems.

Dell said the aim is to separate CPU resources from GPU clusters rather than rely on mixed-use servers, which can complicate power and cooling management. Another system, the Dell PowerEdge R8822, targets more conventional 19-inch rack environments, with support for agentic AI tasks, reinforcement learning, data processing and analytics, as well as up to four double-wide GPUs.

Dell also announced the Dell PowerEdge XE9810 for rack-scale inference. The server will use 16 direct-liquid-cooled compute trays powered by Groq 3 Language Processing Units for high-throughput inference in production AI deployments.

At the network edge, Dell is working with NVIDIA on Aerial RAN Computer platforms running on Dell PowerEdge servers. These are aimed at communications service providers that want radio access network and AI workloads to run on a shared compute footprint rather than on separate systems.

Michael Dell, chairman and chief executive officer of Dell, said: "Enterprises used to think about AI infrastructure as an IT budget question, but that's changed. AI infrastructure is no longer a cost center. It's a value creation center. Companies are expanding and reallocating budgets because AI infrastructure drives growth, productivity and competitive advantage. Together with NVIDIA, we are giving enterprises the integrated platforms they need to move agentic AI from experimentation to results, on infrastructure they own and control."

Jensen Huang, founder and chief executive officer of NVIDIA, said: "AI agents reason, use tools and learn-and they need a new kind of computer. Together, Dell and NVIDIA are building the computing foundation for the age of AI-from the deskside to the data center-so companies can build and run AI agents securely at industrial scale."

Matt Kimball, vice president and principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, said: "The market is entering a new phase where customers are focused less on building AI infrastructure and more on generating measurable business outcomes. The continued expansion of the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA reflects a mature approach that combines validated solutions, ecosystem integration, automation and services, helping organizations move from pilots to production with greater confidence and less risk."

stories.title: APDCA launches playbook for data centre policymakers
stories.summary: The Asia-Pacific Data Centre Association has issued guidance urging regional governments to coordinate power, water and land use planning ahead of accelerating AI infrastructure demand. The playbook targets policymakers who risk being caught unprepared by deployment timelines.
stories.why_it_matters: Data centre projects now move faster than government planning cycles, creating bottlenecks that add 12-24 months to delivery. APDCA's intervention attempts to synchronize infrastructure timelines across jurisdictions, but its effectiveness depends on whether energy ministries, water authorities and local governments actually share data and delegate permitting authority—a coordination challenge few APAC bureaucracies have solved.
stories.title_zh: APDCA发布data centre政策制定者playbook
stories.summary_zh: 亚太数据中心协会（APDCA）发布指南，敦促区域各国政府在 AI 基础设施需求加速之前协调电力、水和土地利用规划。该 playbook 针对那些可能因部署时间表而措手不及的 policymakers。
stories.why_zh: 数据中心项目现在的推进速度已超过政府规划周期，造成瓶颈使交付时间增加 12-24 个月。APDCA 的介入试图跨司法管辖区同步基础设施时间表，但其成效取决于能源部、水务机构和地方政府是否真正共享数据并下放审批权限——这是亚太地区少数官僚体系已解决的协调难题。
stories.content:
The Asia-Pacific Data Centre Association has launched a white paper for policymakers on data centre investment, setting out a three-pillar framework for governments across the region.

The publication, titled *Maximising the Data Centre Opportunity - A Playbook for Policymakers*, outlines 10 policy steps intended to help governments support sustainable data centre growth while managing pressure on infrastructure and resources.

It focuses on issues that have become more prominent as countries pursue artificial intelligence and broader digital economy programmes. These include access to power, water, land and connectivity, as well as the need for predictable investment settings, skills development and public confidence.

### Three pillars

The framework is organised around three headings: Plan, Provision and Partner. Under Plan, the paper calls on governments to build evidence and coordination so they can prepare for demand before it materialises.

Provision covers approvals processes, infrastructure reliability and policy settings intended to support investment. Partner focuses on cooperation between governments, industry and communities, with an emphasis on skills, trust and longer-term economic value.

The paper draws on the experience of the association's members, as well as policy approaches used in Asia-Pacific and other markets. Each of the 10 steps includes practical examples and questions to help policymakers assess local priorities.

According to the group, the framework can be adapted to markets at different stages of development - from those trying to establish basic conditions for investment, to those managing rapid expansion, and those seeking better long-term outcomes.

### Policy focus

Data centres have become a more visible policy issue in several Asia-Pacific markets as demand for cloud services, digital platforms and AI-related computing has grown. That has led governments to consider how to allocate land, secure energy supply, plan water use and expand connectivity while still attracting investment.

The paper argues that early policy choices can influence not only where projects are built, but also the scale of the economic and social effects that follow. It highlights, in particular, the need to plan for future demand and to coordinate energy and water infrastructure with digital infrastructure needs.

APDCA represents commercial data centre operators in the Asia-Pacific region and aims to contribute to policy discussions about the infrastructure systems needed to support digital growth.

Jeremy Deutsch, Chair of APDCA, said the paper was developed in response to government requests for more practical guidance.

"Governments across the region have told us they want practical examples, not just principles. This playbook is our response: ten policy steps across Plan, Provision and Partner, drawn from the experience of operators that build and run data centres in many markets. We look forward to working with governments to apply it, so that data centre growth delivers lasting benefits for economies and communities," Deutsch said.

stories.title: Hanwha Ocean and ABB partner to develop power systems for floating data centers
stories.summary: Hanwha Ocean and ABB have signed an MoU to develop marine-grade power and control systems for floating data centres, targeting offshore deployment as land availability constraints intensify. The collaboration combines shipbuilding expertise with industrial automation technology.
stories.why_it_matters: Floating data centres shift the industry's most intractable constraint—land and permitting—from terrestrial bureaucracies to maritime regulatory frameworks that are arguably more permissive but less tested at scale. If Hanwha and ABB can solve salt corrosion, submarine cable connectivity and crewing logistics, they open an entirely new site acquisition model that bypasses NIMBY opposition and land speculation in prime markets.
stories.title_zh: Hanwha Ocean与ABB合作开发floating data center电力系统
stories.summary_zh: Hanwha Ocean 与 ABB 签署谅解备忘录（MoU），共同开发适用于 floating data centers 的船用级电力和控制系统，目标是在土地可用性限制加剧的情况下进行 offshore 部署。该合作结合了造船专业知识与工业自动化技术。
stories.why_zh: Floating data centers 将行业最棘手的限制——土地和审批——从陆地官僚体系转移到可能更为宽松但大规模验证较少的海事监管框架。如果 Hanwha 和 ABB 能解决盐雾腐蚀、海底电缆连接和人员配备物流问题，他们将开启一种全新的选址获取模式，绕过核心市场的邻避反对和土地投机。
stories.content:
Hanwha Ocean, a South Korean heavy industries company, and ABB, a Swiss-Swedish multinational technology corporation have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to develop power and control technologies for floating data centers, as demand for AI computing increases pressure on land based infrastructure. The partnership will focus on power system design, reliability and operational controls for offshore data centers, which house servers and supporting power and cooling equipment on floating structures.

According to a press release, Hanwha Ocean will lead the basic design and configuration of the floating data center’s power systems, including standards for power generation equipment using liquefied natural gas (LNG) engines. Under the agreement, which runs through May 2027, ABB will assess electrical system reliability and power quality based on the shipbuilder’s designs and review ways to improve operational efficiency .

Heo Yoon, Executive Vice President and Head, Hanwha Ocean Product Strategy and Technology Institute, told Seoul Economic Daily, “As the AI industry grows, technologies that support stable power supply and efficient operation of data centers are becoming more important, through this partnership with ABB, we will raise the technical maturity of floating data center solutions suited to marine environments and broaden the foundation for growth in our future offshore business.”

Hanwha Ocean, which unveiled its in-house floating data center concept at Gastech 2026 in September, will contribute its offshore engineering and construction expertise. ABB will bring its experience in electrification, automation and data center power systems.

The companies will also examine how LNG engines and electrical systems can respond to fluctuations in power demand as AI workloads change. Managing these variations will be critical to maintaining a stable electricity supply and reliable operations in offshore environments.

The agreement reflects growing interest in offshore infrastructure as a way to address the energy and land requirements of expanding digital services as the concept offers a potential alternative to land-based facilities facing constraints in securing suitable sites and electricity.

stories.title: South-east Asia's haze shows a diversified electricity source may not be that dependable
stories.summary: As countries grow reliant on power from across borders, how much will be available when several need it at once?
stories.title_zh: 东南亚雾霾显示多元化电力来源可能没那么可靠
stories.content:
As countries grow reliant on power from across borders, how much will be available when several need it at once?

\[SINGAPORE\] On Oct 9, 2026, Singapore’s Pollutant Standards Index reached 192. The haze was choking throats and clouding skies.

Less visibly, it was also dimming solar panels: Operators in the city-state reported daily average electricity output falling by around 15 per cent during the episode.

It did not lead to an electricity shortage here. But as more South-east Asian countries prioritise generating and trading low-carbon electricity, the episode offers a glimpse of a challenge they face – that suppliers might face the same risks in power generation.

## Different sellers, same sky

When shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted from early March, several Asean members limited air-conditioning and rationed fuel simultaneously: one choke point, many countries.

The lesson drawn is to diversify, including through domestic renewables and electricity traded with neighbours.

Singapore has conditionally licensed six electricity-import projects from Indonesia, totalling 3 gigawatts (GW); all six pair solar generation with battery storage. By 2035, the city-state aims to import around 6 GW of low-carbon electricity from the region.

Other South-east Asian countries are also planning new cross-border connections under the Asean Power Grid.

These links can improve reliability, but they additionally make neighbouring countries more dependent on one another. The catch is that global choke points are not the only risk countries can have in common. Neighbours tend to also share each other’s weather.

In dry years, Cambodia has suffered power shortages at home, and so has Laos, the region’s biggest electricity exporter. El Nino brings hot, dry conditions to much of the region at once, increasing the risks of fires and haze.

The projects in Indonesia involve different developers, but a widespread smoke plume can affect solar generation for weeks across multiple sites.

Haze can also increase electricity demand. In a study of Singapore households, economist Alberto Salvo found that residential electricity consumption increased by about 1.1 per cent for every 10 micrograms per cubic metre increase in fine particulate pollution.

People may use more electricity to cope with polluted air, just as solar panels produce less.

## When everyone needs the same electricity

Electricity that is readily available in an ordinary year may be much harder to obtain in a regional crisis.

Consider an electricity exporter facing a prolonged shortage. It has obligations to deliver electricity to a neighbouring importer, but its consumers also need power.

Meeting its export commitments may become increasingly costly, as domestic supplies tighten.

At the opening of Singapore International Energy Week on Oct 26, Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) Tan See Leng warned: “When there is a supply crunch, countries may also prioritise their own domestic needs.”

He was discussing energy security broadly, including fuel supplies.

The electricity the importer most needs may also be the electricity the exporter finds most costly to spare.

As the International Energy Agency noted in a report in October, after this year’s fuel disruptions, governments that protect their consumers in a crisis can leave import-dependent neighbours short.

The region needs clearer arrangements for such moments – not just for fuel, but also for electricity trade.

For electricity, the existing arrangements are mostly commercial contracts, written to secure financing; banks usually want more than 15 years of revenue certainty before funding a cable. They establish delivery obligations and remedies for interruptions.

But compensation for undelivered electricity does not keep the lights on by itself. Bankable is not the same as dependable. In a regional shortage, replacement power may be scarce or expensive, whatever the contract says.

Different countries may also plan to rely on the same backup supplies during an emergency. Each country’s plan can look reasonable on its own, even if those plans cannot all work at once.

## What counts as dependable electricity?

None of this argues against regional electricity trade. Connections between countries remain valuable, especially when shortages are confined to one place.

The challenge is to distinguish electricity available in normal conditions, from electricity that can be relied upon when several countries face scarcity together.

Import proposals are already tested for bankability. The bad year needs a test of its own. Singapore assesses the resilience of its electricity imports, and Asean’s integrated resource and resilience-planning framework provides a foundation for examining regional risks.

But countries must assess whether their plan still holds when a bad year hits all of them at once: hot, dry weather and a fuel shock together.

The plans cannot all hold where several countries are counting on the same limited imports or reserves. Those are also the places where agreements need clearer terms on what is cut first and where replacement supply comes from.

Such a test needs data shared across borders. Asean already issues seasonal outlooks for haze. Europe’s grid operators publish reservoir levels and forecasts of wind and solar output.

A seasonal electricity outlook for the region would combine the two, and is a foundation to gauge whether national plans in Asean can all hold at once.

Singapore’s 2027 Asean chairmanship offers an opportunity to advance that work with regional partners.

The real test of South-east Asia’s electricity trade is not how much power crosses borders in good times, but how much remains available when supplies run short and countries must balance domestic needs against their commitments to neighbours.

**The writer is a research fellow at the Energy Studies Institute, National University of Singapore**

stories.title: AirTrunk advances plans for proposed Mickleham data centre
stories.summary: AirTrunk has progressed planning for a multi-building campus at Mickleham in Melbourne's northern growth corridor, emphasizing local employment and supply chain benefits. The project represents AirTrunk's continued expansion in the Victorian market beyond existing facilities.
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne's northern suburbs are becoming a contested zone between data centre developers and residential planners. AirTrunk's community-focused messaging signals recognition that social license matters, but the real test comes when power substations and diesel backup generators arrive—local councils in Australia have recently killed projects at far smaller scales than what AirTrunk typically builds.
stories.title_zh: AirTrunk推进Mickleham拟建数据中心计划
stories.summary_zh: AirTrunk 已推进在墨尔本北部增长走廊 Mickleham 建设多栋园区式数据中心的规划，强调当地就业和供应链效益。该项目代表 AirTrunk 在现有设施之外继续扩张维多利亚州市场。
stories.why_zh: 墨尔本北部郊区正成为数据中心开发商与住宅规划者之间的争夺地带。AirTrunk 以社区为重点的信息传递表明其认识到社会许可的重要性，但真正的考验在于变电站和柴油备用发电机到位之时——澳大利亚地方议会最近否决的项目规模远小于 AirTrunk 通常建设的规模。
stories.content:
AirTrunk has proposed a new data centre campus at 45 Donnybrook Road, Mickleham, bringing the potential for long-term jobs, local business opportunities and investment in Melbourne’s north.

The proposal is expected to support more than 1,000 ongoing local jobs and create further opportunities for workers, suppliers and businesses during construction. Subject to the necessary approvals, AirTrunk is also proposing a $26.5 million investments into local community infrastructure, skills and education, including:

- $6.5m to a Victorian Skills Partnership to support the electrical and technical workforce needed for data centres, energy infrastructure and broader electrification.
- $5m to the delivery of local sporting and recreation infrastructure to support community participation and wellbeing.
- $15m for education and training facilities in the Mickleham area, helping local residents learn and study closer to home.
- An expanded Social Impact Program in Melbourne’s northern suburbs, providing ongoing support through partnerships in education, biodiversity and conservation, and digital inclusion.

The campus has been designed to use air-based cooling and would not use community water for cooling during normal operations. The site is more than 400 metres from the nearest home, with the design intended to screen equipment and minimise noise beyond the site.

AirTrunk will fund the infrastructure required to connect the campus to the Victorian transmission network. We are committed to matching its electricity use with renewable energy and is exploring opportunities to support new renewable energy projects.

AirTrunk is holding community information sessions and a webinar in November to share details about the proposal and hear feedback on local opportunities, community benefits and construction impacts.

“We want to engage with people who live and work in Mickleham and the surrounding area,” said Rob Bartrop, Associate Vice President of Social Impact & Community at AirTrunk.

“We’re committed to keeping the community informed, creating opportunities for people to participate in the training, employment and procurement opportunities, and to investing into much-needed community infrastructure in Melbourne’s northern suburbs.”

The proposal is subject to planning and environmental approvals. More information, including details of consultation opportunities, is available at airtrunk.com/mickleham.

stories.title: Equinix opens SG6 data centre in Singapore for AI demand
stories.summary: Equinix's SG6 facility brings 8 MW and 1,550 cabinets online in Singapore, where land and energy constraints are tightening as AI workloads surge. The expansion reflects ongoing pressure on the city-state's limited data centre quota system.
stories.why_it_matters: Singapore's data centre market is becoming a zero-sum game: every new MW approved requires someone else to wait or go elsewhere. Equinix securing capacity signals that incumbents with existing footprints can still expand, but newcomers and smaller players face steeper barriers. This will push more AI demand into Johor, Batam and other secondary markets.
stories.title_zh: Equinix在新加坡开设SG6 data centre以满足AI需求
stories.summary_zh: Equinix 的 SG6 设施在新加坡上线，提供 8 MW 电力和 1,550 个机柜，而当地土地和能源限制正因 AI 工作负载激增而收紧。此次扩张反映出新加坡有限的数据中心配额制度持续面临压力。
stories.why_zh: 新加坡的数据中心市场正变成零和博弈：每批准一个新的 MW，就意味着其他人必须等待或转向别处。Equinix 获得容量表明，已有布局的 incumbents 仍能扩张，但新进入者和较小玩家面临更高壁垒。这将推动更多 AI 需求流向 Johor、Batam 及其他次级市场。
stories.content:
Mon, 9th Nov 2026 (Today)
Equinix has opened its SG6 data centre in Singapore, its sixth facility in the city-state.

The new International Business Exchange facility is aimed at AI, high-density computing and other data-intensive workloads. It adds 8 MW of capacity in its first phase and about 1,550 cabinets, with total IT capacity expected to reach 20 MW when fully built out.

Equinix has invested about USD $290 million in the project. SG6 is also among the first data centres developed under Singapore's Data Centre Call for Application framework.

Singapore has become a closely watched market for data centre operators as limits on land and energy use, along with tighter sustainability standards, coincide with rising demand for cloud and AI infrastructure. The new facility is intended to serve businesses operating across Asia-Pacific from one of the region's most connected hubs.

SG6 includes liquid-cooling arrangements and other cooling systems designed to support power-intensive graphics processing unit infrastructure. It also combines private interconnection with access to Equinix's wider network of customers and partners.

### Sustainability focus

The site is designed for a Power Usage Effectiveness rating of 1.20 and is targeting Green Mark Platinum certification. It also includes rooftop and facade solar photovoltaic systems, rainwater harvesting, and construction materials intended to lower embodied carbon.

Equinix said its Singapore data centres have maintained 100% renewable energy coverage since 2020. SG6 also forms part of the group's broader targets of reaching net zero emissions by 2040 and full renewable energy coverage across its retail IBX estate by 2030.

Singapore is now one of Equinix's densest interconnection hubs in Asia-Pacific. The company entered the market in 2002 and has expanded from one site to six, linking customers in sectors including cloud, information technology, financial services, communications, media, and technology.

Its facilities in the city-state also provide access to global markets through more than 17 subsea cable systems, underlining Singapore's role as a regional gateway for digital traffic and business connectivity.

"Singapore sits at the intersection of global commerce, digital technology and sustainable development," said Adaire Fox-Martin, Chief Executive Officer and President of Equinix. "Equinix has been investing in Singapore for nearly 25 years, and our new facility will further expand our presence as the neutral exchange where enterprises connect to the clouds, networks and partners they need to innovate and grow. Singapore is one of our most important markets globally, and our continued investment here is a testament to the central role it plays in the digital economy."

Regional demand for data centre capacity has been rising as businesses increase spending on AI systems, cloud services and digital operations. Operators across Asia-Pacific have been adding capacity while facing pressure from governments and customers to improve efficiency and limit environmental impact.

Equinix said Singapore remains a strategic market because of its concentration of enterprises, network providers and international links. The company is also planning a Co-Innovation Facility at SG6 with the National University of Singapore, focused on data centre sustainability and energy efficiency research, including liquid cooling, cognitive digital twins and battery energy storage systems.

"Asia-Pacific is at the forefront of digital transformation, with AI adoption, cloud expansion and data-intensive workloads driving unprecedented demand for high-performance digital infrastructure," said Cyrus Adaggra, President, Asia-Pacific, Equinix. "Singapore remains a strategic gateway for businesses serving the region, connecting key markets, talent and innovation ecosystems. SG6 strengthens our ability to support customers as they scale across Asia-Pacific, providing the resilient, interconnected and sustainable infrastructure they need to accelerate innovation and capture new growth opportunities."

stories.title: What a data centre will do to Kurri Kurri
stories.summary: AirTrunk has published community-facing materials addressing local concerns about energy, water, traffic and noise impacts from its proposed Kurri Kurri data centre in regional New South Wales. The outreach reflects broader industry efforts to secure social license outside metropolitan areas.
stories.why_it_matters: Regional Australian communities are becoming more sophisticated in negotiating with data centre developers, moving beyond initial enthusiasm for jobs to demand concrete commitments on water recycling, local procurement and post-construction community funds. AirTrunk's proactive disclosure sets a benchmark that will become table stakes for subsequent projects, raising the cost and complexity of community engagement but potentially reducing cancellation risk if executed genuinely.
stories.title_zh: 数据中心将对Kurri Kurri产生什么影响
stories.summary_zh: AirTrunk 发布了面向社区的材料，回应当地对其拟议的新南威尔士州地区 Kurri Kurri 数据中心的能源、水、交通和噪音影响的担忧。这一外展反映出行业在都会区之外争取社会许可的更广泛努力。
stories.why_zh: 澳大利亚地区社区在与数据中心开发商谈判时正变得更加老练，从最初对就业机会的热情转向要求水循环利用、本地采购和建设后社区基金的具体承诺。AirTrunk 的主动披露为后续项目设定了基准，这将提高社区参与的成本和复杂性，但如果真诚执行，可能降低取消风险。
stories.content:
### By Rob Bartrop – AirTrunk Associate Vice President, Social Impact & Community

Across regional Australia, people are paying ever increasing attention to the growth of data centres. People are asking reasonable questions about energy and water, traffic and noise, and what the long-term impacts might be on daily life.

Those concerns deserve to be heard.

At AirTrunk, we have spent months listening to the Kurri Kurri community – through community consultation sessions, a drop-in centre on Lang Street, and dozens of conversations with local businesses, sporting clubs, community organisations and interested residents.

Much of that work has been about understanding concerns and making sure they are reflected in the project we have proposed.

But there is another question we think is equally important.

**What will actually be different in the day-to-day lives of people who live here?**

Our view is that, if we get this right, Kurri Kurri will be a stronger community because of the project.

**That starts with something tangible: 350 good, long-term operational jobs and genuine pathways for people to find work.**

In a region experiencing significant workforce transition, particularly as people look towards new careers beyond traditional industries, that matters.

These are opportunities for people to build a career close to home, with the potential for well-paid, full-time employment across a wide range of roles. And through a long-term partnership with Kurri Kurri Community Services, we want to support young people aged 14 to 17 who have disengaged from mainstream education – providing a pathway back towards opportunity, confidence and employment.

We expect that program to support around 20 to 30 young people each year, which will hopefully impact hundreds of young people and their families over decades to come.

We are also partnering with Hunter Trade College and TAFE to create scholarships, placements and other opportunities for young people looking to build practical skills and enter the workforce.

**A $37m contribution to local infrastructure that will provide lasting benefit.**

The project will contribute to the delivery of major local infrastructure improvements, including a multipurpose community facility and two new playing fields at Loxford. We have heard repeatedly from local junior sporting organisations in Kurri that access to playing fields is a constraint, and that Cessnock City Council can’t find the funds to provide them.

For a local parent, that means something very simple: more opportunities for children to play sport closer to home.

**It also means stronger sporting organisations.**

Kurri Kurri is home to several historic clubs that are run largely by volunteers and play an enormous role in bringing people together. Our multi-year partnerships with local sporting organisations are intended to help those clubs continue to thrive, including supporting the Kurri Kurri Bulldogs to introduce a women’s team and ensuring junior programs can continue to grow and become more affordable for the local soccer and rugby league clubs

The same principle applies to the organisations that support people when they need it most.

We are making a significant commitment to the Cessnock District Rescue Squad, including the provision of a new four-wheel-drive rescue vehicle to support volunteer rescuers across the area. This will be the first such vehicle to be made available to a Rescue Squad outside of a major city.

**And there is another benefit that is much closer to home: household energy costs.**

Through our proposed community energy program, around 5,000 homes across Kurri Kurri, Heddon Greta and Weston would be able to participate in our Community Energy Program, with eligible households able to receive a credit of up to $200 a year on their electricity bills that is enabled through our funding of a local community battery.

For families, that is not an abstract benefit. It is money that stays in the household.

Yes, the community is entitled to ask hard questions about data centres. We should expect that scrutiny, and we should continue to listen and respond.

But we should also realise that all of these opportunities have been embedded in the delivery plan for the Kurri Kurri data centre project.

In other words, a Kurri Kurri that is stronger, more connected and better equipped for the future.

That is the opportunity we see in this project – and it is the standard we believe we should be held to.

You can find out more information about our Kurri Kurri Data Centre Project **website**.

stories.title: Lam, imec advance 3D integration, dry resist for AI computing
stories.summary: Lam Research and imec have extended their strategic collaboration to advance 3D integration and Aether dry resist technologies. This work supports future AI logic, memory, and heterogeneous integration, enabling performance gains for AI computing.
stories.title_zh: Lam与imec推进用于AI计算的3D集成和dry resist技术
stories.content:
Lam Research and imec have extended their strategic collaboration to advance next-generation 3D integration and Aether dry resist for high-NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) patterning. This joint research aims to enable future artificial intelligence (AI) logic, memory, and heterogeneous integration technologies.AI models demand unprecedented computing power, memory bandwidth, and energy efficiency, the companies said. Meeting these requirements increasingly depends on how chips are designed, connected, packaged, and manufactured as complete systems.Three-dimensional integration, advanced packaging, next-generation memory, and new patterning technologies are critical enablers for AI computing. These allow chipmakers to overcome traditional scaling constraints and deliver necessary performance gains.Lam and imec are collaborating to accelerate manufacturing readiness for 3D integration technologies. This supports advanced packaging and next-generation memory architectures.The collaboration combines Lam's deposition and etch capabilities with imec’s integration infrastructure. This aims to boost the speed at which innovations move from lab to high-volume manufacturing.Joint research areas include thick dielectric deposition, asymmetric stress compensation, bevel deposition, and plasma dicing. The work also covers process validation for advanced packaging and future memory architectures.It extends into future 3D memory technologies, such as new charge-trap materials and precision multilayer deposition. High-aspect-ratio channel etch, deep memory contacts, and low-resistivity interconnects are also part of the focus.These innovations are crucial as AI workloads drive demand for greater memory density and bandwidth.
### Advancing High-NA EUV Patterning

AI also relies on continued advances in leading-edge logic devices, the companies noted. High-NA EUV lithography is required to enable smaller features and increased transistor density for angstrom-era nodes.Lam and imec are advancing the application of Lam's Aether dry resist platform for high-NA EUV patterning. This joint work uses imec's high-NA EUV research environment.The focus is on enhancing resolution, sensitivity, depth of focus, and stochastic defectivity. The collaboration explores Aether-enabled patterning for advanced interconnects, including ruthenium direct metal etch.These innovations support lower-resistivity interconnects and improved electrical performance for future logic nodes. Joint research achieved single-exposure high-NA EUV patterning for sub-20 nm ruthenium direct metal etch interconnects.This work obtained 100 per cent electrical yield for fork structures sensitive to bridges. It also achieved over 90 per cent for meander structures sensitive to breaks at 20 nm pitch.Aether-enabled patterning could reduce multi-patterning complexity and improve manufacturability. Aether is part of a broader approach to enabling gate-all-around (GAA) and complementary FET (CFET) architectures for future AI computing.

- AI & Compute Infrastructure
- 2 min Read

stories.title: Data centre rush needs a $5b electricity upgrade in South Australia
stories.summary: South Australia requires an estimated A$5 billion in electricity grid upgrades to support surging data centre demand, according to industry and government assessments. The investment need underscores the mismatch between renewable-heavy generation and baseload reliability requirements.
stories.why_it_matters: South Australia's grid was designed around intermittent renewables and demand-side management, not continuous multi-hundred-MW loads. The A$5 billion figure forces a reckoning: either taxpayers subsidize infrastructure for predominantly foreign-owned hyperscalers, or data centre operators accept higher costs and longer timelines that could redirect investment to Queensland or New South Wales with more robust coal and gas backup.
stories.title_zh: 数据中心热潮需要南澳50亿澳元电力升级
stories.summary_zh: 据行业和政府评估，南澳大利亚需要约 50 亿澳元的电网升级以支持激增的数据中心需求。这一投资需求凸显了以可再生能源为主的发电与 baseload 可靠性要求之间的错配。
stories.why_zh: 南澳大利亚的电网是围绕间歇性可再生能源和需求侧管理设计的，而非持续性的数百 MW 负载。50 亿澳元这个数字迫使各方正视现实：要么纳税人补贴基础设施以服务于主要由外资拥有的 hyperscalers，要么数据中心运营商接受更高成本和更长工期，这可能将投资转向拥有更强大煤电和天然气后备的昆士兰州或新南威尔士州。
stories.content:
A proposed $5 billion upgrade of electricity grid transmission capacity in South Australia would only be finished by 2032, casting doubt on the prospects of almost 30 data centre proposals being considered in the state.

The early-stage proposals are concentrated in remote locations to ward off rising community backlash, making the planned 500-kilometre upgrade of high-voltage electricity lines and substations by the state’s electricity transmission network owner ElectraNet crucial to their plans.

stories.title: Stockland scraps Sydney data centre plans after local backlash
stories.summary: Stockland has withdrawn its Sydney data centre proposal following sustained community opposition, marking another instance of local resistance blocking AI infrastructure in Australian metropolitan areas. The abandoned project reflects intensifying scrutiny of data centre impacts on residential neighborhoods.
stories.why_it_matters: Australian data centre development is hitting a social license ceiling in established suburbs, forcing developers toward industrial zones or regional areas with weaker grid connections and longer approval paths. Stockland's retreat signals that even mixed-use developers with deep community engagement experience cannot overcome localized NIMBYism, suggesting pure-play data centre specialists may face even steeper hurdles unless they fundamentally redesign site selection and community consultation processes.

stories.title_zh: Stockland因当地反对放弃悉尼数据中心计划
stories.summary_zh: Stockland 在持续的社区反对后撤回了悉尼数据中心提案，这是本地阻力阻止澳大利亚都会区 AI 基础设施的又一案例。被放弃的项目反映出对数据中心影响住宅区的审查日益加剧。
stories.why_zh: 澳大利亚数据中心开发在成熟郊区正遭遇社会许可上限，迫使开发商转向工业区或电网连接较弱、审批路径更长的区域地区。Stockland 的撤退表明，即使是拥有丰富社区参与经验的混合用途开发商也无法克服本地化的邻避主义，这意味着纯数据中心专业公司可能面临更陡峭的障碍，除非他们从根本上重新设计选址和社区咨询流程。
stories.content:
(Nov 8): Stockland Corp has abandoned plans for a Sydney data centre following community backlash, in another sign of growing opposition to artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The property developer said the nearly two-square-kilometre logistics project on a former golf course next to Sydney Airport, a joint venture with John Boyd Properties, will “not include a data centre” in its next stage of planning. “We will continue to engage openly with stakeholders as planning for the logistics precinct progresses,” a company spokesperson said.

First announced last year, the development on the banks of the Cooks River has sparked criticism from community groups after data centres were added as a potential alternative use earlier this year. The company had said that the project’s proximity to the airport and nearby Port Botany made it suitable for mixed uses like retail and hospitality.

Community opposition to data centres is growing across Australia on concerns over their heavy power and water use. Last month, data centre company Nextdx Ltd placed development plans on hold after protests delayed power supply to one of its major projects in Melbourne.

Firmus Grid Ltd also faced backlash against its planned data centres. The company was set to debut on Australia’s stock market last month, but shelved plans after failing to win over investors for its US$30 billion valuation.

stories.title: Asia: Stocks follow US gains, Nvidia probe looms
stories.summary: Asian equities rose alongside US markets, though investor attention is fixed on regulatory scrutiny of Nvidia export approvals under the Trump administration. Questions persist about enforcement rigor for advanced chip sales to certain markets.
stories.why_it_matters: Markets are pricing in two conflicting signals: bullish AI infrastructure demand and rising geopolitical friction over chip controls. Any tightening of export enforcement would immediately hit Nvidia's Asia-Pacific revenue and ripple through data centre buildout timelines in China-adjacent markets, while lax enforcement risks political backlash in Washington.
stories.title_zh: 亚洲：股市跟随美国上涨，Nvidia调查逼近
stories.summary_zh: 亚洲股市随美股上涨，但投资者注意力集中在特朗普政府对 Nvidia 出口批准的监管审查上。关于向特定市场出售 advanced chips 的执法严格程度，疑问依然存在。
stories.why_zh: 市场正在消化两个矛盾信号：看涨的 AI 基础设施需求和芯片管制加剧的地缘政治摩擦。任何出口执法收紧都将立即冲击 Nvidia 的亚太收入，并波及邻近中国市场的数据中心建设时间表；而执法宽松则可能引发华盛顿的政治反弹。
stories.content:
Attention now turns to US inflation data Tuesday for clues on the rate outlook

\[HONG KONG\] Asian stocks opened higher following Friday’s (Nov 6) gains in US equities, though advances were tempered by concern over an investigation involving Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang.

The MSCI Asia Pacific Index climbed 0.7 per cent, with Japan’s Nikkei 225 Stock Average rising 1.9 per cent. A gauge of US semiconductor shares jumped 4.2 per cent on Friday as speculation about possible tighter Democratic Party regulation of the artificial intelligence industry eased.

Equity-index futures for the Nasdaq 100 Index dropped as much as 1 per cent after Nvidia’s board said it was launching an investigation into whether Huang had been targeted in a foreign espionage plot following his admission that he was unfaithful to his wife.

Brent crude declined 0.4 per cent to around US$97.90 a barrel after US President Donald Trump said it was “highly unlikely” he will order further strikes on Iran if progress is made in talks over its nuclear programme and the reopening the Strait of Hormuz, CNN reported.

The dollar weakened against most of its Group-of-10 peers, while New Zealand’s currency strengthened following a national election over the weekend. Bitcoin advanced 1.3 per cent to trade close to US$75,000.

“The Nvidia honey trap will weigh on Asian markets to kick off the week,” said Nick Twidale, chief market analyst at AT Global Markets. “It just creates huge uncertainty over what happens over Nvidia which is one of, if not the biggest, AI company out there.”

The probe into Huang threatens to further dent already-fragile risk appetite after a rout in richly valued technology shares pushed Japanese and Taiwanese stocks into technical bear markets last week and sent a gauge of global equities to a six-month low. Investors are also assessing the US midterm results and their implications for fiscal policy, regulation and growth.

In Asia, Chinese consumer and producer price data Monday will offer the next read on the health of the world’s second-largest economy. Inflation may have picked up in October because of higher energy costs, according to Bloomberg Economics.

Attention now turns to US inflation data Tuesday for clues on the rate outlook, with traders assigning an almost 80 per cent probability of a hike by year-end.

“History is awash with examples of what – ex post – look like reckless risk-taking, and the verdict on AI is still out,” Barclays strategists led by Themistoklis Fiotakis wrote in a note to clients.

“That said, solid growth momentum and the likely extension of the capex cycle without massive downward revisions make us inclined to buy any dip in the dollar.” BLOOMBERG

stories.title: Nvidia probes whether CEO Huang was target of foreign intelligence effort
stories.summary: US intelligence agencies are examining whether foreign intelligence services, with particular attention from China, have targeted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The probe highlights growing concerns about executive security at semiconductor firms central to AI supply chains.
stories.why_it_matters: If foreign intelligence is actively targeting chip company leadership, the personal security calculus for executives across the semiconductor and AI infrastructure sectors shifts dramatically. Companies may need to harden executive protection programs, and governments could impose new travel and disclosure restrictions that complicate deal-making and partnership-building across borders.

stories.content:
Nvidia is probing whether CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, after a media report alleged he had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing.

Huang admitted in a message to employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife and took "full responsibility" for his actions, while Nvidia said the CEO was committed to continuing to lead the company without interruption.

*The New York Times* reported last month that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, whom US authorities were investigating.

US authorities have scrutinised Megaspeed, which buys AI chips from Nvidia, over suspicions it helped Beijing gain access to advanced AI chips that are barred from shipment to China.

"The Nvidia board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

"A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation," Nvidia said.

The company said that, while its board has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry will examine all available information.

Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, it added.

The investigation adds to pressure on Nvidia at a time investors are already pulling back from uncertainty over the sustainability of the AI market, in which the company is a leader. 

The US$4.5 trillion ($6.6 trillion) chipmaker's shares have given up all their gains this year amid a broader tech market rout triggered by worries over AI sustainability.

Huang admitted to having been unfaithful to his wife, saying, "My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

Addressing his colleagues, board, partners and shareholders, Huang said: "My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence."

Top Republican lawmakers in the US House of Representatives have called on Huang to brief Congress this month about the report.

The report raises "significant national security concerns regarding (China's) access to sensitive US technology and information," the lawmakers said in a letter dated November 4.

"It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk," they added.

Huang, who founded Nvidia in 1993, said that he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security."

Nvidia had earlier said that Huang talks with "thousands of customer executives every year," and that cloud customers in Asia receive ordinary business information, not sensitive Nvidia trade secrets or anything tied to US national security.
